items.title: Woman's family wrongly told she was dead in hospital identity error
items.description: A Melbourne hospital apologises after mixing up the medical data of two people, resulting in one of them being wrongly declared dead by police.

items.title: 'Police every day': How school is different for Jewish Australian kids
items.description: The Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion hears from Jewish school leaders about how they need to implement extraordinary and expensive security measures.

items.title: 'Not finished': Trump signals US strikes on Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site
items.description: President Donald Trump says the United States is far from finished with Iran, warning its next military target could be an underground nuclear complex known as Pickaxe Mountain.

items.title: Family of seven's home left uninhabitable as insurer worsens damage
items.description: A Queensland family are living in an overcrowded caravan and shed, after insurance provider Suncorp exacerbated damage in their home, initially caused by a leak.

items.title: Labor members revive push for national gambling watchdog
items.description: Labor members and unions are gearing up for fights over gambling, gas and AI at the party's national conference later this week.

items.title: Albanese's career mirrors Howard's in two important ways
items.description: Anthony Albanese has been in near-fatal vehicle accidents not once, but three times. Politically, his is also a story of survival against the odds.

items.title: Map reveals Australia's 'pharmacy deserts' are not all in the bush
items.description: Australia's "pharmacy deserts" have been mapped for the first time, revealing remote NT communities and outer-city Melbourne have fewer pharmacies per person than some other parts of the country.

items.title: Victorian teachers are going on strike again — here's what you need to know
items.description: Victorian state school teachers and educators are going ahead with their second 24-hour strike this year after union members rejected the government's latest pay offer.

items.title: Who paid for Pauline Hanson's trip to Europe? Not taxpayers, she says
items.description: In her first appearance since returning to Australia, Pauline Hanson fields questions about her trip to Europe with billionaire Gina Rinehart.

items.title: 'Irresponsible': Russia conducts live-fire weapons exercise off British coast
items.description: A UK minister has confirmed that a Russian naval vessel conducted a "live-fire weapons exercise" in international waters off the coast of Plymouth in south-west England.

items.title: AI company plan to use irrigation water disappears after ABC question
items.description: Data centre builder Firmus Technologies posts to its website a statement, since removed, indicating its intention to get some of its cooling water from the state-owned irrigation system, adding "but we do not want to highlight this yet, as they are yet to agree".

items.title: AI companies 'stole' Australian culture, news bosses say, as they call for licensing deals
items.description: The heads of the ABC, SBS, Nine and News Corp say AI companies should strike licensing deals rather than freely train on Australian news, warning journalism is a public good that must be protected.

items.title: Iran war delays upgrades to Queensland’s Triple Zero phone system
items.description: The Iran war has been a contributing factor to Queensland's Triple Zero phone system being delayed until next year, the ABC understands.

items.title: The 'precious' bond driving the Stingers to success
items.description: Australia's women's water polo team, the Stingers, were the most successful Australian team at the Paris Olympics, winning a stunning silver medal. This is the secret to their success.

items.title: JackJumpers coach shares advice on how to win over Tasmanians
items.description: Being out amongst the people will be key for incoming Tasmania Devils coach Ken Hinkley, according to the man who led the state to NBL glory in 2024.

items.title: Travel quiz: join us for a trip around the world
items.description: Where are macadamia nuts indigenous to? And what’s the capital city of Switzerland?

items.title: New Ozploitation horror is like Puberty Blues from hell
items.description: After spending years in special effects and make-up, filmmaker Mia'Kate Russell's ocker nightmare Penny Lane Is Dead has made it to the silver screen.

items.title: Seized scam centre in Myanmar offers rare glimpse into industry targeting Australians
items.description: The scam industry in Myanmar is morphing and heading into the jungle rather than disappearing since a crackdown began.

items.title: Falling objects at BlueScope trigger breaches months after death
items.description: There have been six incidents involving falling tools and building materials at BlueScope, less than a year since contractor Jack McGrath was killed.

items.title: Sixteen-year-old in custody suspected of killing mother, injuring little sister
items.description: Police say a teenage boy is suspected to have stabbed his mother to death and seriously injured his 12-year-old sister in an alleged family violence homicide in Perth's south-east.

items.title: UK politician Ann Widdecombe hit 21 times with hammer, prosecutors allege
items.description: Joshua Kerry, 28, appears in the Westminster Magistrates' Court charged with murder over the killing that has shocked the public and political establishment.

items.title: Job system broken for workers, booming for private equity, report says
items.description: A new report argues Australia's employment services system is failing jobseekers, while filling the pockets of private equity firms and millionaires.

items.title: Mother of identical quadruplets calls them her 'miracle babies'
items.description: A maternal foetal medicine expert believes identical quadruplets born in Brisbane may be even rarer than one in 15 million, given they shared a placenta.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby child protection review finds departmental failings
items.description: Nearly three months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, an interim report into her family circumstances prior to the tragedy has been handed down.

items.title: Police confirm investigation involving incident with NT administrator
items.description: Former army commando turned Labor MP, Luke Gosling, has denied involvement in an alleged incident with King Charles's representative in the NT.
